title: Learjet 60: Four Tires, One Decision After V1 — What the NTSB Found (Columbia, 2008)
description:
September 19, 2008, just before midnight at Columbia Metropolitan Airport, South Carolina: a Learjet 60 (N999LJ) rejects its takeoff after V1 and overruns runway 11. Explained second by second, only with the NTSB final report NTSB/AAR-10/02 and its cockpit voice recorder transcript.

This is NOT the Learjet 60 that crashed near Greenacres, Florida, on Nov. 1, 2026 — that investigation is still open and the NTSB has not determined its cause. Nothing in this video is an explanation of that crash.

The NTSB determined that the probable cause of the 2008 accident was the operator's inadequate maintenance of the airplane's tires, which resulted in multiple tire failures during takeoff roll due to severe underinflation, and the captain's execution of a rejected takeoff after V1, which was inconsistent with her training and standard operating procedures. Contributing factors listed by the NTSB include deficiencies in the design and certification of the Learjet 60 thrust reverser system, which increased the severity of the accident.
